findings.summary: The name argument is interpolated into the JSON template without escaping, so a value containing a double quote injects arbitrary JSON fields (demonstrated: an attacker-supplied role:admin key), and backslashes or control characters produce invalid JSON.

The range check uses shell arithmetic with 64-bit wraparound, so 18446744073709551666 wraps to 50 and is accepted as a valid page size, and leading-zero inputs are parsed as octal or raise a base error.

The ownership check fails open on empty principals: calling it with an empty caller and empty owner returns success and prints the value, so a failed owner lookup plus an unauthenticated caller grants access.
The storage backend name is executed as a program with no allowlist or existence check, which becomes arbitrary program execution if the value is ever config or request derived.
Locking is correct under concurrency, but a corrupted non-numeric counter file is silently reset to 1 rather than reported as an error, and the lock file is never cleaned up.
